title: Dasara Rush Chokes Hyderabad-Vijayawada Highway as Queues Build at Pantangi Toll
excerpt: Festival traffic, a school holiday through October 22 and unfinished flyover work at Choutuppal combined to slow NH-65 to 20-40 minutes on short service-road stretches.
body:
• The Dasara exodus choked the Hyderabad-Vijayawada highway (NH-65), with long queues at the Pantangi toll plaza in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district.
  • Flyover and underpass construction at Choutuppal is pushing traffic onto narrow service roads, where short stretches are taking 20 to 40 minutes.
  • Vijayadashami falls on October 20 and Telangana schools are closed October 10-22; on peak days Pantangi handles more than 1.3 lakh vehicles.
  • APSRTC is running 5,261 special buses for the festival: 3,207 from October 16-19 and 2,054 for the return from October 20-25.

The Dasara rush choked Hyderabad's exits on Saturday as thousands of residents drove to their hometowns for the festival, with long vehicle queues forming toward Vijayawada at the Pantangi toll plaza on National Highway 65, according to Telangana Tribune.

Construction Meets the Exodus

The worst delays are at Choutuppal, where flyover and underpass works, part of a long-pending project to fix accident-prone black spots, push vehicles onto narrow service roads. Short stretches there now take 20 to 40 minutes to cross. Bottlenecks were also reported from Dandumalkapur to Valigonda, Hyderabad Mail reported.

https://x.com/TOIHyderabad/status/2111425311506411666

Police opened additional toll booths and diverted vehicles through alternative routes around the construction zone. Ministers had earlier directed that key flyovers on the corridor be completed before the festival season; work at some locations remains unfinished.

Why This Weekend

Vijayadashami falls on Tuesday, October 20, and schools in Telangana are closed from October 10 to 22, giving families a long window to travel to native places across Andhra Pradesh. On peak days the Pantangi plaza handles more than 1.3 lakh vehicles, and festival jams on NH-65 are a recurring pattern, seen every Sankranti as well.

Authorities have tried technology at this bottleneck before: satellite-based toll collection was tested at Pantangi on a trial basis to clear vehicles faster, the Tribune noted. The recurring festival gridlock, despite extra booths and trials, is why the unfinished Choutuppal works carry political weight beyond one weekend.

The Bus Alternative

The Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation is operating 5,261 special buses for Dasara, 3,207 of them from October 16 to 19 for the outbound rush and 2,054 from October 20 to 25 for the return, serving Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai routes as well as pilgrim destinations, according to The Hindu via Scoopfeeds. The main festival days run from Durgashtami on October 18 and Maharnavami on October 19 to Vijayadasami on October 20.

Inside Hyderabad on Sunday

The festival weekend also brings Saddula Bathukamma celebrations to Hyderabad on Sunday, October 18, with traffic diversions around Tank Bund and Necklace Road from 2 pm to 11 pm, Hyderabad Mail reported. Police will divert general vehicles at Telugu Talli Junction, Iqbal Minar, the VV Statue at Khairatabad, Nallagutta Junction, Liberty and Karbala Maidan in Secunderabad, routing traffic via Indira Park, Gandhinagar and RTC X Roads. Residents staying in the city should plan around the Tank Bund closure window.

What's Next

The return rush will hit the same narrowed corridor from October 20 onward. Travellers driving back to Hyderabad face the same Choutuppal service roads in reverse, and officials expect the toll plaza queues to build again through October 25.
